purpose: Literal research inputs for stages 16–23 and 32. Each trace is a separate initial state. Steps are ordered; flags are observations at that step. No driver or physical fixture was run.
conditions: All six BOM selections unless scoped by case. Assume exclusive access to the selected sensor, stable power, timely complete MSB-first word transfers and no intervening conversion except where a step specifies otherwise. Software admission, retention and publication expectations follow docs/prompts/ENGINEERING.md.

sources.page_numbering: One-based pinned PDFs in docs/reference/manifest.json. A named page group applies to every row in the referencing case.

timing.units: Milliseconds. PDF pages are one-based. CC denotes continuous conversion.
timing.interpretation: Each matrix cell is the published nominal total CC period, including active time. A block that fills or exceeds the selected period has zero standby. The active-time tuples are separate count multiplications of the single-conversion row. Their typical values (15.5, 124, 496, 992) preserve unrounded arithmetic. The averaged bounds assume successive equal-condition conversions with no extra block overhead. TI gives no CC maximum period.

TMP116.electrical_condition: One active conversion. Limits at 1.9 to 5.5 V and -55 to +125 C; typical at 3.3 V and +25 C.

TMP117.electrical_condition: One-shot mode. Applying the electrical row to a continuous block is an estimate. Table conditions: 1.7 to 5.5 V at -55 to +70 C, or 1.8 to 5.5 V at -55 to +150 C; typical at 3.3 V and +25 C. The selected grade retains its own specified operating range.

TMP119.electrical_condition: Single conversion without internal averaging. Table conditions: 1.7 to 5.5 V at -55 to +70 C, or 1.8 to 5.5 V at -55 to +150 C; typical at 3.3 V and +25 C. The selected grade retains its own specified operating range.

policy.source: Library choices for the polling and timing-origin contracts in docs/prompts/6_timing-status.md and ENGINEERING.md. Stage 9 owns the full deadline contract.
policy.clock: Use the authoritative monotonic clock at transfer completion. Examples use exact tick-aligned events unless specified. For a wait d after a known tick-aligned completion t, the due tick is t + ceil(d/q)*q for clock step q. If t is a floor-clock reading with unknown sub-tick phase, use t + q as the upper bound on physical completion before adding the rounded wait. The fixed deadline still covers preflight, waits, callbacks and result acquisition.
policy.continuous: The nominal conversion-window budget is max(1.25 * cycle, active upper estimate) + 10 ms. Default readiness checks are separated by one nominal cycle from the verified generation baseline or last completed poll. An overdue poll can run once if budget permits; never replay missed polls. An untimed attempt has caller-owned pacing.
policy.one_shot: Use active upper estimate + 10 ms for a default conversion-window budget, independent of CONV. First poll follows successful trigger completion by the rounded-up active upper estimate. If ready is clear, pace subsequent polls from the completed poll. No retrigger. The 10 ms slack is finite and cannot guarantee that a late owner or a slow bus can finish.
policy.deadline: conversion_window_budget_ms is the unrounded default duration used to size the conversion portion of a whole-operation budget. Round that duration up to clock resolution when deriving a default cap. The schedule cases state any caller-selected whole-operation cap explicitly. An operation must separately admit all required preflight and terminal transfers under its absolute cap. A due time past the deadline expires without a transfer. Clip every callback to the remaining budget and resample after it. A late physical success supplies only observed evidence and its physical transport outcome.
policy.precision: An explicit earlier latency poll can overlap active conversion. A CC cycle can have zero standby. No policy controls traffic from other bus users or proves precision or completion. See SNIS236 p.23.

schedule_cases.conditions: TMP117 in verified shutdown, AVG=00, CONV=111. Operation-local guard and SD baseline succeeded. Owner admits a 35 ms whole-operation budget.
schedule_cases.expect: No poll before 122 and no fresh sample at 122 solely from time. A ready observation on the next poll permits one TEMP read if budget remains. CONV=000 gives the same waits.

schedule_cases.conditions: TMP119 AVG=11, CONV=000. The guarded SD baseline and trigger succeeded within the original deadline; the caller chose a shorter whole-operation cap.
schedule_cases.expect: Due exceeds the cap; zero readiness or TEMP reads, no sample and no second trigger. Elapsed time or the 1000 ms nominal CC cell cannot prove completion.

schedule_cases.conditions: TMP116 AVG=00, CONV=000. The verified baseline is retained from a prior apply at t=100. The guarded read operation starts then, with a caller-supplied 50 ms cap. The owner services the first poll late.
schedule_cases.expect: No readiness poll before t=116. Pace from actual poll completion after each zero. t=156 is outside the cap; zero further reads and no sample.

sources: SNOSD82D p.6, pp.12-14, p.28 table 7-7 row 000
schedule_cases.conditions: TMP117 AVG=11, CONV=000. The continuous active upper value extrapolates the one-shot row. Baseline at t=0, one-ms clock. The full operation has an explicit 1260 ms cap.
schedule_cases.expect: The first poll can overlap active conversion. Expire without the second poll. A zero cannot quantify missed completions.

sources: library deadline and read-effect policy in ENGINEERING.md
schedule_cases.conditions: TMP117. A guarded CONFIG readiness poll is due. The callback reports success after its clipped timeout. The configured callback budget was 8 ms.
schedule_cases.expect: Track one physically successful read, retain HIGH and ready observations with destructive-read provenance, and report logical timeout. Zero TEMP reads; preserve last-good sample.

reset_and_serial.por: Each electrical reset row specifies a typical time. During the approximately 1.5 ms power-up load, reads can succeed; ignored-write wording covers all registers on TMP116 and CONFIG/limits on TMP117/TMP119. Offset behavior during load is unknown.
reset_and_serial.busy_conflict: SBOS740A p.17 gives cleared busy during loading; CONFIG p.26 and unlock p.29 give asserted busy during power-up/loading. Neither a compatible ACK nor a clear busy bit independently proves load completion.
reset_and_serial.serial_condition: Electrical serial-timeout limits concern SDA release without clock. The 35 ms typical prose specifies controller-held SCL low or sensor-held SDA low between START and STOP. SNOSD82D labels the timing table fast-mode; SNIS236 prints the limits under fast-mode. Expiry resets the serial interface. Callback timeout and absolute operation deadline are independent.

origin_cases.conditions: TMP116 begin with no prior proof, assured stable power through use, clock step 1 ms. Compatible ID read launched at 10 and completed at 12.
origin_cases.expect: No managed write before t=15. At or after t=15 require this operation's 0x04 locked/idle read, then verify affected stable fields after writes. A prior bind or caller timestamp cannot advance this boundary. Unknown power stability refuses mutation.

origin_cases.conditions: TMP117, clock step 1 ms. Guarded addressed reset succeeded. Discard old proof before the command. Recovery uses a new compatible ID read, then the startup guard.
origin_cases.expect: Read 0x04 at or after t=56. EUN=1 refuses all subsequent writes. Neither the 2 ms reset interval nor the separate policy wait establishes relock or EEPROM reload. TMP116 has no corresponding command.

origin_cases.conditions: TMP117 with stable power. The driver sees whole milliseconds rounded down. Fractional times are visible only to the test observer. The original deadline is tick 57.
origin_cases.expect: Tick 52 gives only 1.1 ms after reset. Read no earlier than tick 53. The compatible read completes before tick 54, so the 3 ms FIRST_ACK wait permits the guard at tick 57. With zero remaining budget, issue zero guard reads and zero writes.

temperature_and_limits.condition: Signed two's-complement counts, 1/128 degree Celsius per count. The encoding also applies to THIGH (0x02) and TLOW (0x03). Endpoints are arithmetic limits.

host_quantization.condition: Example host policy for finite in-range requested limits and offsets: nearest count, ties away from zero. Rejection emits no register word. TI specifies the format; internal averaging rounding remains unknown.

offset_result.condition: TMP117/M/N and TMP119 only. Each row follows observed completion with a known offset. Add signed counts after linearization and saturate the reported result. These rows have no expected comparator order.
offset_result.tmp116_gate: A managed offset request on TMP116/N has zero transfers. Its 0x07 is EEPROM3 (SBOS740A pp.24,30).

pin_routes.condition: One device, working pullup, ordered limits, no outside ARA. For each row, complete an in-range conversion with HIGH=LOW=0 (A), acknowledge CONFIG, complete an above-THIGH conversion and read TEMP (B), then read CONFIG again (C). At A DATA_READY=1. At B and C DATA_READY=0. The addressed CONFIG read at C clears alert-mode HIGH; therm HIGH stays asserted. Physical H means released/pulled high and L means sinking. GPIO sampling is illustrative and supplies no freshness proof.

traces.condition: Start after POR in CC with AVG=01. Inputs are synthetic signed counts per conversion; each complete eight-count mean is exactly representable. Readiness is initially clear.

steps.event: read TEMP twice with no intervening block

traces.condition: Alert mode, AVG=00, initially clear. Verified THIGH=0xFCC0 (-6.5 C), TLOW=0xFAC0 (-10.5 C). HIGH/LOW in each comparison row are hardware flags after completion. The final external ARA uses threshold routing, POL=0 and a working pullup.

traces.condition: Therm, AVG=01, initial HIGH=0, TLOW=0xFAC0, THIGH=0xFCC0, no reset. Comparisons use completed block results explicitly on TMP117/M/N and TMP119. Block-end comparison on TMP116/N is inferred from result update and comparator text.

resume; change POL/DR route while retaining therm mode and no completed comparison

traces.condition: Verified desired SD stable bits 0x0620, AVG=8, alert mode, startup proof. All managed transfers occur under exclusive ownership. Example old and new results may be equal. Read only the listed fields of observed CONFIG.
traces.alternate: For an above-high completed block, the readiness poll captures HIGH before acknowledging it. If subsequent TEMP fails, suppress the result, retain HIGH for exactly one explicit alert consumption and flag possible lost readiness. An in-range block does not assert a threshold event just because the one-shot prose mentions ALERT (SNOSD82D p.15, SNIS236 p.17).

traces.condition: Each row is independent. Unless specified otherwise, desired SD and the remaining stable fields match. Documented SD abortion does not require any particular MOD readback during or after an owned shot.

traces.condition: Repeat separately for a limit-only change, a routing/polarity-only change and AVG/CONV changes. Old generation G is verified in CC. Both generations use alert mode. A conversion can complete as soon as CC restarts.

traces.alternate: A failed or mismatched final readback leaves the profile dirty and supplies no new trusted baseline. If that CONFIG instead matches stable fields but reports EEPROM_Busy, record its read effects and invalidate the guard. Resume guarded verification only after a safe 0x04 read within the deadline. A single discarded block after a live settings rewrite has unknown provenance.

traces.condition: Reported TMP117 continuous-mode interleaving. The author describes DATA_READY routing on bit 2 but quotes 0x0040. Table 7-6 assigns DR/Alert to 0x0004 and 0x0040 to AVG. Actual configuration, applicability to other models and the exact internal clear edge remain uncertain.

traces.policy: No catch-up count or time-only publication. Loss of an owned one-shot indication can end in timeout without retrigger. A combined two-byte TEMP read is required; the source gives no byte-latching rule for an overlapping continuous update.

traces.addressed_reset: TMP116/N refuses before I/O. On TMP117/M/N and TMP119 invalidate old proof before the guarded reset command is attempted, honor the separate 2 ms reset interval and establish new post-reset FIRST_ACK and guard before dependent writes. Re-observe lock, fields and shadows; addressed reset load, lock, other written bits and bus availability lack explicit guarantees.

traces.condition: F13. An earlier owner may have customized EEPROM or its volatile shadows. Arbitrary example words at 0x05 and 0x06 apply to all selected BOM models.

steps.event: after fresh startup proof, observe reloaded shadows

traces.policy: Either zero or nonzero words can be observed. Read-only observations cannot identify an immutable serial, establish NVM contents or authenticate calibration. Driver writes to EEPROM data words or their shadows: zero.
